title: CoinRun PPO historical re-evaluation and all-old combined control
question: Does the exact combination of the old CR-PPO-0001 training settings reproduce a policy-quality collapse under the same evaluator, or was the historical low score caused by evaluation identity or another source/runtime difference?
reason: The CR-PPO-0003 single-factor arms seen so far do not collapse. A generic interaction explanation is insufficient: the historical 6.29M checkpoint and a fresh all-old combined run must be compared under byte-identical evaluation identity.
hypothesis: If the old settings have a nonlinear combined effect, both the historical checkpoint and a fresh all-old combined run will score at least 1.0 mean return or 0.10 success rate below the CR-PPO-0003 reference under the same final-256 evaluator.
falsification: Reject a reproducible combined-settings collapse if the fresh all-old combined arm remains within both margins of the reference. If only the historical checkpoint is low, investigate historical source/runtime identity or run variance; if its same-metric re-evaluation is not low, attribute the original gap primarily to evaluation identity.

controlled_variable.name: checkpoint_or_training_recipe
values: fresh all-old combined settings at 6,291,456 transitions

source.source_freeze: The preregistration, evaluator, runner, summarizer and tests were committed and pushed at 31ebeee1830dc14ec58d6c79fb3a0ff2989b189c before either CR-PPO-0004 result.

compute.estimated_budget: One 256-episode checkpoint re-evaluation plus one fresh 6,291,456-transition arm, expected roughly 20-25 minutes.
compute.shutdown_policy: Reuse the same bounded A10 only after CR-PPO-0003 terminates; no concurrent GPU training.

success_criteria.rule: Historical, reference and fresh combined metrics all match 6,291,456 transitions and the same stochastic full-distribution 256-episode evaluation identity.
Call a collapse only when mean return is at least 1.0 lower or success rate at least 0.10 lower than the CR-PPO-0003 reference.
Do not call settings a software bug unless a code or runtime contract violation is independently demonstrated.
No trajectory collection or dynamics training starts.
